paper.title: Bellman-Centric Learning: Near-Optimal Regret for Linear Bandits with Memory

unmapped: Reward is <a_t, A(s_t) theta*> where memory state s_t = last M actions (known memory length M); deterministic known state transitions induced by the learner's own actions (endogenous nonstationarity)
the learner knows the memory map A: A^M -> R^{dxd}, with sup operator norm <= R; the learner knows R
regret is measured against the optimal length-T action sequence (policy regret) from the same initial memory
settings.definition_quote:
Specifically, the observed reward is
\begin{equation}\label{eq:reward_function}
    y_t = \left\langle a_t,A(s_t)\theta^\star\right\rangle +\varepsilon_t.
\end{equation}
The reward parameter $\theta^\star$ is unknown and satisfies
$\theta^\star\in\Theta\coloneqq \{\theta\in\mathbb{R}^d:\|\theta\|_2\leq S\}$. The memory map
$A:\mathcal{S}\to\mathbb{R}^{d\times d}$ is known a priori and uniformly bounded in operator norm: $
\sup_{s\in\mathcal{S}}\|A(s)\|_{\mathrm{op}}\leq R. $ The noise sequence $(\varepsilon_t)_{t\geq1}$ is
conditionally zero-mean and $\sigma$-sub-Gaussian given the history and the current action.

unmapped: Reward depends on memory state of last M actions through known memory map A with operator norm <= R (sup over A taken in minimax)
learner knows the memory map A and R
regret against optimal length-T action sequence (policy regret)
settings.definition_quote:
Suppose $d\geq2$ and \(T\geq d\max\left\{ M,1,\sigma^2d/\left(48R^2S^2\right) \right\}.\) There exists an
admissible action set such that the minimax regret of \model{} satisfies
\[
    \inf_{\pi} \sup_{\substack{ \theta^\star:\ \|\theta^\star\|_2\leq S\\
    A:\ \|A\|_{\mathrm{op}}\leq R }} \mathbb E\left[\operatorname{Reg}_T(\pi)\right]
    \geq \Omega\big(dRS(M+1)+\sigma d\sqrt T\big).
\]

unmapped: Natural parameter z = <A(s)^T a, theta*> with memory state of last M actions and known memory map A (||A||_op <= R)
canonical exponential family with known dispersion v and known link mu, twice differentiable with mu'>0 and |mu''| <= rho mu' on [-RS,RS]; learner knows v, rho, kappa, U_mu, R
regret against optimal length-T action sequence (policy regret)
settings.definition_quote:
Unlike \model{}, where the conditional reward mean is $z(s,a)$, \gmodel{}
models the reward through a known canonical exponential family~\citep{lee2024glm, liu2024almost,
anngeneralized}. Specifically, an observation $y$ at $(s,a)$ has density or probability mass function
\[
    \mathbb{P}[y\mid z(s,a)] = \exp\left( \frac{yz(s,a)-b(z(s,a))}{v}+c(y,v) \right),
\]
where $v>0$ is the known dispersion parameter which controls the noise level of the observed reward, and
$\mu(\cdot)=b'(\cdot)$ is the known link function.

settings.name_in_paper: Generalized linear bandits with memory (GLBM) (lower bound)
unmapped: Memory-dependent generalized linear reward with known memory map A (||A||_op <= R); learner knows v, rho, link mu
regret against optimal length-T action sequence (policy regret)
settings.definition_quote:
Let $d\geq3$, $M\geq 0$, and
\(T\geq\max\big\{dM,d,\frac{v(d-1)^2}{U_\mu}\max\left\{\frac{1}{4R^2S^2},\rho^2\right\}\big\}\). Then there
exists an admissible action set such that
\begin{equation}\label{eq:glbm_lower_bound}
    \inf_{\pi}\sup_{\theta^\star,A} \mathbb E\left[\mathrm{Reg}_T(\pi)\right] \geq \widetilde\Omega\Big(
    d(M+1)\Delta_\mu +d\sqrt{vU_\mu T} \Big).
\end{equation}

If \(T\geq\frac{v(d-1)^2}{U_\mu}\max\left\{\frac{1}{4R^2S^2},\rho^2\right\}\), there exists an admissible action set such that, with $A(s)=RI_d$ for every $s$, every policy $\pi$ satisfies \sup_{\theta^\star} \mathbb E[\mathrm{Reg}_T(\pi)] \geq \frac{3(d-1)}{16\sqrt e}\sqrt{vU_\mu T}.
